data.hypothesis: Transposing B once per process makes each output dot product read both operands contiguously; an OpenMP SIMD reduction over k may improve vectorization while preserving the exact integer-valued results.
data.notes: Transpose allocation and construction remain part of end-to-end runtime. Products and all partial sums are exact integers within the valid input bounds, so SIMD reduction reassociation does not change results. Performance is unmeasured; transpose overhead may dominate small inputs.
transformations: Allocate and build a transposed copy of B once, outside the repeats loop.
Compute each output with a dot product over contiguous rows of A and transposed B.
Enable an OpenMP SIMD reduction over the independent dot-product accumulation; retain strict compiler math settings and existing output behavior.
